clue.text: Remote inland area? Favour coastal locations

parts.note: a boon is a favour or blessing
docks are harbour places on the coast

explanation.surface: Someone asks a favour of seaside places while musing about the remote interior.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose, informal definition: the word is North American slang for the back country.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang term, chiefly American, for rough, isolated country far from towns.

clue.text: Is gossip circulating? That's for me!

indicators.note: going round, so these words are turned back to front

parts.note: gab is idle chatter or gossip

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether rumour is spreading, then grabs something for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' turns the pieces round. The answer is a British children's call for claiming something first.
explanation.definitionFit: Playground claim phrase used to reserve something for oneself before anyone else can.

clue.text: Unable to supply favourite items, slipping up, misreading the Zeitgeist

parts.note: a shop that is out of something cannot supply it

indicators.note: in a down light, going up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in teacher's pets

explanation.surface: A shop runs out of popular stock and blunders, failing to catch the mood of the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipping up' reverses PETS to give STEP, the word read upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for being at odds with current fashion or prevailing opinion.

clue.text: Enclosed yard after end of year? It's the right thing to do

definitions.text: It's the right thing to do

indicators.note: the letters for enclosed and yard follow the month

parts.note: December, abbreviated Dec, is the year's final month
enc. is the standard abbreviation for enclosed, on letters

explanation.surface: A walled yard at year's end prompts musing about proper behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of year' is not the last letter R but the last month, DEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Propriety or seemly conduct is acting in a fitting, respectable way.

clue.text: Husband overwhelmed by better bloke

indicators.note: being overwhelmed means being surrounded, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: A husband is outdone by a superior fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a man or fellow.

clue.text: One studying fish with floating marker, we hear

parts.note: a school is a group of fish

indicators.note: the word for the marker is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a buoy is a float marking a channel

explanation.surface: Someone studies fish beside a buoy bobbing in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' makes BUOY sound like BOY.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil at school is someone engaged in study.

clue.text: Dispose of crown in trench

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a sap is a covered siege trench
CR is the abbreviation for Crown

explanation.surface: A king throws away his crown in a ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: To discard or throw out something as unwanted.

clue.text: Veteran accommodated by senior member of forces

indicators.note: being housed by something puts one piece within the other

parts.note: an oldie is an old-timer, a veteran

explanation.surface: An old campaigner is put up by a high-ranking officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'senior member' reads as one phrase, but 'senior' is SR and 'member of forces' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A serviceman in an army is a member of the armed forces.

clue.text: Show minister revolution in Evangelical Union?

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a minister's title

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: EU are the initials of Evangelical Union

explanation.surface: A clergyman reveals an upheaval within a church body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution in' turns EU into UE.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical entertainment of sketches and songs is a kind of show.

clue.text: Minuscule creatures ruined America (Pennsylvania first)

indicators.note: the state abbreviation is placed at the front

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tiny organisms have spoiled America, starting with one state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges AMERICA into RAMECIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Single-celled slipper-shaped protozoans, microscopic pond organisms.

clue.text: Upset at charges? Try to get in for free

definitions.text: Try to get in for free

indicators.note: being upset means being knocked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at entry fees tries to sneak in without paying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' rearranges AT CHARGES.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend a party or event uninvited, without paying or permission.

clue.text: One enjoys part of Test after 50

indicators.note: the cricket term follows the numeral

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50
an over is a set of six balls in a cricket Test match

explanation.surface: A cricket fan relishes a passage of a Test match after a half-century.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six deliveries in cricket; a Test is an international match.
explanation.definitionFit: A devotee or enthusiast is someone who enjoys a thing.

clue.text: Actually having name for Catholic child

indicators.note: the phrase gets a replacement letter
one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: in fact means actually

explanation.surface: Someone really has a name chosen for a Catholic baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having name for Catholic' swaps the C of IN FACT for N.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby or very young child, especially in British schools the youngest age group.

clue.text: Love music broadcast (with volume cut) from London opera house

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are rearranged
a cut removes something, here the letter for volume

explanation.surface: Romantic music is aired with the sound turned down from a London venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with volume cut' removes V from LOVE MUSIC; 'broadcast' rearranges the rest, LOEMUSIC. The London Coliseum is home to English National Opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre in London's West End, home of English National Opera.

clue.text: Irascible character in children's book

definitions.meaning: the water rat in The Wind in the Willows

explanation.surface: A grumpy figure from a children's story.
explanation.walkthrough: The water vole in Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritable and touchy is the informal British sense; also a famous water vole's name.

clue.text: Important broadcaster's run ending in despair after "Farewell and thank you"

indicators.note: the final letter follows the farewell and thanks

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
adios is Spanish for goodbye
ta is British slang for thank you

indicators.note: the last letter of the word that follows is taken

explanation.surface: A major presenter's career ends in gloom after a goodbye and thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending in despair' gives R. The phrase echoes the song 'Video Killed the Radio Star'.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity of the wireless era is a prominent broadcasting personality.

clue.text: Outside Cancer or Capricorn, but mostly Scorpio, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals another arrangement of these letters
most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Star signs: not Cancer or Capricorn but probably Scorpio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last O of SCORPIO; 'possibly' rearranges BUT SCORPI. Cancer and Capricorn are tropics, not star signs.
explanation.definitionFit: Regions bordering the tropics lie just beyond the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn.

clue.text: Boats, to me, must be wrecked here!

definitions.text: Boats, to me, must be wrecked here!

indicators.note: wrecking smashes things up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sea-captain predicts that boats are bound to founder at this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be wrecked' rearranges BOATS TO ME; the whole clue describes where sunken boats end up.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocean floor is where shipwrecks come to rest.

clue.text: Funny old man to gasp, heading off for bar

parts.note: to pant is to gasp for breath

indicators.note: the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a saloon is a bar

explanation.surface: An amusing old fellow gasps as he heads off to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the S from SALOON. The figure is the foolish old man of commedia dell'arte and pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock comic character in Italian commedia: a foolish, doddering elderly figure.

clue.text: International negotiations see qualification appended to country's boundaries

indicators.note: added at the end, so the edge letters follow

parts.note: a diploma is an academic qualification

indicators.note: the boundaries are the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: Talks between nations involve a certificate attached to a state's borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country's boundaries' gives C and Y, the outer letters of 'country'.
explanation.definitionFit: Conducting relations between states through talks is statecraft.

clue.text: Remove old book (volume 1) at end of range

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone takes away an old book, the first volume, from the end of a shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of range' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude or make unnecessary, getting rid of a need or difficulty.

clue.text: Cheers after month in government

indicators.note: the thanks come after the month

parts.note: Jun is the abbreviation for June
ta and cheers both mean thanks in British slang

explanation.surface: Applause after a month in office.
explanation.definitionFit: A military group ruling after seizing power is a form of regime.

clue.text: Magistrate is nothing but formality

parts.note: just means merely, nothing but
ice is coldness or stiff reserve of manner

explanation.surface: A judge is all stiff ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formality' is ICE in the sense of chilly reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A justice of the peace is a lay judge, a local magistrate.

clue.text: Former 5 almost angry about lack of fame

parts.note: 5 down is a schoolboy, and a former one is an Old Boy, OB

indicators.note: the last letter is left off

parts.note: livid means furious
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: An ex-pupil, nearly cross, complains about his obscurity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost angry' gives LIVI. An Old Boy is a British term for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Being forgotten or unknown is the state of obscurity.

clue.text: Useless object of Parisian dismissed by French paper

indicators.note: something dismissed is sent away, so these letters go

parts.note: Le Monde is a French daily newspaper
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A Parisian's worthless item is rejected by a French newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Parisian' is DE, the French for 'of', removed from LE MONDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dud or defective item, especially a faulty car, is a useless thing.

clue.text: Tense after literary lion's giving oblique view

indicators.note: the tense letter goes after the lion

parts.note: Aslan is the lion in C S Lewis's Narnia books
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A tense moment follows a famous fictional lion offering a sideways look.
explanation.definitionFit: At an angle or slanting, not straight or perpendicular.

clue.text: Meeting expectation after unknown takes over university

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: trust is confident expectation
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A meeting is anticipated after a stranger seizes a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unknown takes over university' replaces the U of TRUST with Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret romantic rendezvous between lovers.

clue.text: Expression of pleasure hard work's worn down

indicators.note: worn at the bottom, so the last letter of this down entry goes

parts.note: a grind is tedious hard work

explanation.surface: A smile from someone ground down by toil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn down' trims the last letter, D, from GRIND.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad smile shows on the face when happy.

clue.text: American city tending to back accepting American

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece goes inside
going back means the letters are reversed

parts.note: apt to means inclined or tending to

explanation.surface: A US city tends to back an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives TPA, which takes the second 'American' inside; the first belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Florida city on the Gulf coast.

clue.text: Slip with the very thing before over in Test ground

indicators.note: these go inside the word for test

parts.note: to try is to test

indicators.note: these come before the over letter

parts.note: to err is to slip up
it means the very thing, as in 'that's it'
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A cricket mishap, a slip, before an over at a Test match ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip', 'over' and 'Test' all look like cricket terms; here they are ERR, O and TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: An area of land or domain is a region of ground.

clue.text: Material from sewer in sea water?

indicators.note: the letters are drawn out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Waste from a sewage pipe ends up in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material from' picks letters out of 'sewer in sea'. The question mark marks 'water' as a verb in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash lightly with clean liquid, as in rinsing dishes.

clue.text: Thousand accepted by financial expert as seed

indicators.note: being accepted means being taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: money nut, a nut being an enthusiast or expert in money matters

explanation.surface: A finance guru accepts a thousand as a starting sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'financial expert' is jocular: a nut is a devotee, so a money nut. The answer is the British name for a peanut.
explanation.definitionFit: A peanut is the edible seed of a legume.
